2. Heard Sri Anil Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Rajeev Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the first informant as well as Sri V.K.S. Parmar, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 257 of 2022, U/S 498A, 304B, 328 IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Fatehgarh Kotwali, District Farrukhabad, during the pendency of trial.
4. As per prosecution story, the marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the deceased person as per Hindu rites on 29.4.2017 and a baby boy was born out of the said wedlock.

The applicant and other co-accused persons are stated to have subjected her to cruelty for a demand of dowry leading Birendra Singh @ Chhotu vs State Of U.P. on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84869066/

sentences.text: 5. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that the applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.

Learned counsel has stated that the house of the sister of the informant (deceased)
and the applicant were in the same lane and it was the love marriage and no dowry was exchanged between the parties.
Learned counsel has stated that the child is being taken care of by the parents of the applicant.
Learned counsel has also submitted that the deceased was several times instigated by the family members that their reputation has been tarnished in the vicinity owing to the said marriage.
Learned counsel has further stated that this might have led the sister of the informant to commit suicide.
Learned counsel has also submitted that it is also evident that about 4-5 hours before her death, she had gone to her maternal home and has consumed some poisonous substance there.

Learned counsel has placed much reliance on the statement of several neighbours of the deceased person, who have stated that the relation between the two was not cordial as the applicant is stated to be a drunkard.
The said neighbours also corroborated the story of the parents of the deceased person saying bad words to her daughter (deceased).
It is next stated that in all, four persons were named in the FIR and the police had exonerated other three accused persons and filed a closure report with respect to them.
No cause of death has been ascertained and the viscera has been preserved.
There is no FSL report furnished by the prosecution to date.

It is next stated that the expenditure of the treatment meted out to the deceased person was borne by the father of the applicant namely, Santosh Pal, which is evident from Annexure-8 annexed to the bail application.
6. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
It is further stated that there is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 1.8.2022.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the first informant have vehemently opposed the bail application on the ground that the inquest report categorically indicates that none of the neighbours were present there and the bill of the treatment having been undertaken by the father of the applicant does not stand verified.

Learned counsel has further stated that the deceased had expired within the precincts of the house of the applicant by consuming some poisonous substance and the applicant and other persons had run away from the scene of occurrence at the said time of incident.

8. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties, nature of offence, evidence on record, pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, and taking into consideration the said facts elucidated to be some poisonous substance that the deceased has consumed within the precincts of the house of the applicant and expired there, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
this Court is not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
